title: Quick Revision: How do Organisms Reproduce?
subject: Science

bullets: DNA copying passes on the body design. Small copying errors cause **variation**, which helps a species survive when the environment changes.
Reproduction keeps populations stable in their niches.

table: Splits into many cells at once, inside a cyst
Breaks into pieces, each grows into a new organism
Body pieces grow into complete organisms (specialised cells)
New plants from roots, stems or leaves
Bryophyllum (leaf notches), potato eyes, rose cuttings, grafting, layering

blocks.p: **Vegetative propagation advantages:** grows plants that don't make viable seeds (banana, orange, rose, jasmine); flowers and fruits come earlier; offspring keep the parent's good characters. **Tissue culture** grows many plants from a few cells.

bullets: Stamen (male): anther + filament. The anther makes **pollen**. Pistil (female): stigma, style, ovary with ovules (each ovule has an egg cell).
**Pollination:** pollen reaches the stigma. Self-pollination is in the same flower; cross-pollination is to another plant (by wind, water or animals).
Pollen tube grows through the style to the ovule. Male germ cell + female germ cell → **zygote** (fertilisation).
After fertilisation: zygote → embryo; ovule → seed; ovary → fruit. Petals, sepals and stamens shrivel and fall.
**Puberty:** sex hormones (testosterone, oestrogen) bring changes in the body.
**Male:** testes make sperm and testosterone (they lie outside the body because sperm need a lower temperature). Vas deferens carries sperm. Seminal vesicles and prostate add fluid.
**Female:** ovaries release one egg a month and make oestrogen and progesterone. Fertilisation happens in the **oviduct**. The embryo implants in the **uterus**.
**Placenta:** villi give a large surface area for glucose and O_{2} to pass from mother to embryo, and wastes to pass back. Gestation is about 9 months.
No fertilisation: the uterus lining breaks down and comes out as menstruation (about every month).

box: **Contraception:** barrier (condom, which also protects against STDs), hormonal (oral pills), copper-T/loop in the uterus, surgical (vasectomy / tubectomy).
**STDs:** gonorrhoea and syphilis (bacterial), warts and HIV-AIDS (viral).
